decisions.rationale: 'Prader-Willi syndrome' is a named genetic disease with one specific definition, so it is a Specific Disease using the whole phrase as the minimum necessary span.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease); What to Annotate 5 (minimum necessary span)

decisions.rationale: 'PWS' is the abbreviation of Prader-Willi syndrome and is annotated as a separate synonymous mention referring to the same specific disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 6 (synonymous mentions); What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease)

decisions.rationale: 'neurogenetic disease' refers to a family of multiple specific genetic neurological diseases rather than one defined disease, so it is a Disease Class.
'infantile hypotonia' is a clinical sign or symptom (low muscle tone) describing a feature of PWS, not a disease name, and is not a disease mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 4 (general terms); What to Annotate 1 (disease mentions only)

decisions.rationale: 'gonadal hypoplasia' describes a clinical feature/abnormality associated with PWS rather than a named disease entity, so it is not annotated.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 4 (general abnormality-type terms excluded)

decisions.rationale: 'neonatal feeding difficulties' is a symptom description and a general clinical term rather than a specific disease mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 4 (general terms such as complications and abnormalities)

decisions.rationale: 'hyperphagia' is a symptom (excessive eating) describing a feature of the syndrome, not a disease mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 4 (general terms); What to Annotate 1 (disease mentions only)

decisions.rationale: 'obesity' is a recognized disease entity with a defined meaning that is not further categorized here, so it is annotated as a Specific Disease.
Here 'PWS' is used as the subject referring to the disease itself ('PWS is due to a lack of paternal genetic information'), a repeated mention of the specific disease that is annotated.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 4 (duplicate mentions); What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease)

decisions.rationale: In 'the PWS region' the abbreviation modifies the noun 'region' and does not denote the disease itself, so it is a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3 (disease mentions used as Modifiers)

decisions.rationale: In 'the PWS IC element' the disease name modifies the noun phrase 'IC element' (imprinting centre element), so it is a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3 (disease mentions used as Modifiers)

decisions.rationale: In 'leads to PWS' the abbreviation refers directly to the disease Prader-Willi syndrome as an outcome, so it is a Specific Disease mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease); What to Annotate 4 (duplicate mentions)

decisions.rationale: In 'a PWS family' the disease name modifies the noun 'family' and characterizes it, so it is a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3 (disease mentions used as Modifiers)

decisions.rationale: In 'the PWS IC element is not only required' the disease name modifies the noun phrase 'IC element', so it is a Modifier.
